overview.title: The town a visitor can find on one map
overview.lead: HelloLocal puts local places, events and the map on a single page. In Hungarian, English and German. An editor publishes it, a guest opens it on a phone. No separate app.
overview.seoTitle: HelloLocal | A town map, its events and its places
overview.seoDescription: Places, events and one shared map in Hungarian, English and German. For municipalities, tourist offices and destinations.
overview.keywords: local tourism, town map, event calendar, tourist office, destination, HelloLocal
overview.shotCaption: Szeged on the map: places, filters and the next events on one screen.
overview.statsLanguages: languages, each with its own address
overview.featuresTitle: What keeps a visitor on the page
overview.featuresLead: Not another brochure. A page where someone decides where to go this afternoon.
overview.stepsTitle: Three steps, and they are already browsing
overview.closingTitle: The next guest is already searching on a phone.
overview.closingText: Open the map, look at the events, and picture your own town's places on those dots.

collect.title: You gather the places
collect.text: A winery, a promenade, a museum, a market. Category, opening hours, a photo and a short text. Each one has an address you can send.

publish.title: You publish the programme
publish.text: The coming weeks sit beside the map. A featured event stays at the top. One that has ended drops off.

share.title: You hand it to the visitor
share.text: One link in Hungarian, English or German. The guest filters, zooms in and sets off. No app store, no account.

app.q: Does a guest have to download an app?
app.a: No. The map and the events open in the browser, on a phone and on a computer.

languages.q: Is there a separate site for each language?
languages.a: Content can be Hungarian, English and German, each with its own address. Search engines can then find it in the right language.

editors.a: Editors and place owners work with their own permissions. Descriptions use a text editor, and sign-in can require a second step.

towns.q: Can several towns share one system?
towns.a: Yes. Each town or destination gets its own content, map and editors. A visitor only sees the one they opened.

places.title: Places worth opening
places.text: Category, price, opening hours and a page a guest can send to the group. Not a spreadsheet: an address, a photo, a reason to go.

events.title: The next event, not last year's poster
events.text: Events line up beside the map, in time order. What has finished comes off. What is featured stays in front.

map.title: A map you can actually leave from
map.text: The dots are the places. Filters show what is open, what is fine in the rain, and where something happens today. On a phone the panel rises from the bottom and the map stays visible.

languages.title: The language the guest searches in
languages.text: Hungarian, English and German content, each on its own address. A foreign visitor gets the same map, not a translated leaflet.

sites.title: Several towns, with clear edges
sites.text: A destination can carry more than one place. Each has its own content, map and editors, so a visitor does not wander into another town's programme.

editors.title: A local editor, not an agency
editors.text: The text is written by someone who knows the place. Roles separate the town editor from the owner of a venue. The change shows up on the public page.

municipality.title: Municipality
municipality.text: The town's events, the promenade and the market finally live on one link, not in three separate social posts.

office.title: Tourist office
office.text: A foreign guest gets the same map in English or German that locals use in Hungarian.

destination.title: Destination and wine region
destination.text: Several towns in one system, each with its own places. The visitor tours the region instead of a mixed list.
